# Ask LLM

> Second opinions for coding agents. Get a second opinion on your code or plan, inside your coding assistant, using the model subscriptions you already have.

For individual developers and small teams who already use a coding assistant and another model subscription. Review changes or challenge a plan without API keys, copy-paste, or leaving the session.

Install on Linux or macOS with Node.js 24+, then select your host and confirm the preview:

```bash
npm i -g @ask-llm/mcp && ask-llm setup
```

Install and sign in to the provider separately. Then ask: “Ask Codex to review my staged changes for bugs and missing error handling.” Choose a reviewer from a different vendor. Calls consume account quota or billing; Grok's metered API is explicit. Local Ollama models are supported. Antigravity refuses by default and opt-in has no read-only guarantee. Ask LLM sends no telemetry. Agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

## Start

### Install

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install.html

Get a second opinion on your code or plan, inside your coding assistant, using the model subscriptions you already have.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 24+ on Linux or macOS. Before your first review, both your coding assistant (for example Claude Code) and the provider you will consult (for example Codex) must be installed and signed in. Ask LLM configures their connection; it does not install providers or sign you in. If a provider CLI such as Codex has never been signed in on this machine, sign in first and rerun setup. See [authentication](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/operation/authentication) if either account is not ready.

## Install and connect

See the install command above; select your host, inspect the preview, and confirm.

Setup discovers hosts separately from providers and asks you to confirm each detected host and workflow. Review the command or file preview, confirm your assistant's registration and workflows, and decline the others. Setup works at user scope, preserves unrelated entries, and prints backup locations and restart instructions. Pairing remains off.

Follow any manual guidance in the output before continuing. Existing Codex registrations require manual inspection because the host's inventory does not prove user-scope ownership. Antigravity needs the printed workflow-copy step. OpenCode registration is tested with fixtures only. See [host compatibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts) and [migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

Start a new session in your project or restart your assistant, then [ask for your first review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/first-review).

## Preview without changing anything

```bash
ask-llm setup --dry-run
```

To target just one assistant, use `ask-llm setup --host claude` (or another [host ID](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/cli#host-ids)). Running setup again preserves compatible registrations and refreshes changed workflows.

If no supported assistant is found, use [manual configuration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/manual-configuration). If setup fails, run `ask-llm doctor` and use [troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting).

### First review

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/first-review.html

Before your first review, both your coding assistant (for example Claude Code) and the provider you will consult (for example Codex) must be installed and signed in. Ask LLM configures the connection; it does not install providers or sign you in. If a provider CLI such as Codex has never been signed in on this machine, sign in first and rerun `ask-llm setup`.

Open a project with a small staged change. With both Claude Code and Codex signed in, ask in Claude Code:

```text
Ask Codex to review my staged changes for bugs and missing error handling. Check each finding against the source before proposing fixes.
```

If Codex is your host, ask Claude instead. You can name any [provider](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install#before-you-start) you have authenticated; choose a different vendor from the model writing the code.

A successful response identifies the reviewer and model and cites code supporting its findings, or says it found none. Your assistant stays responsible for editing. Review the evidence and decide which fixes to apply; agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

If you get a missing-tool or authentication error, run `ask-llm doctor` in your terminal, follow its remediation for your selected assistant and reviewer, and restart the host. Warnings about providers you do not use do not require installing them or adding API keys. [Troubleshooting](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/resources/troubleshooting) covers common failures. Registration alone does not prove a provider can answer.

Next, [review a larger change](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes) or [challenge a plan](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/challenge-plan).

### Upgrade and remove

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/upgrade-remove.html

## Upgrade

Repeat the install line from [Install](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install), then restart the host. Setup preserves compatible registrations and refreshes changed workflows. It previews replacements for earlier registrations and leaves customised entries with guidance; see [migration](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

## Remove registrations

```bash
ask-llm remove
```

Inspect the preview and confirm. MCP removal deletes only registrations whose command resolves to this installation's server. Codex receives manual guidance when ownership cannot be verified. Removal does not restore replaced or retired entries.

Pi removal runs `pi remove` for this installed package's local entry after confirmation; foreign and legacy npm entries and local entries with custom filters stay in place. The Claude Code plugin and portable skills remain installed. Removal prints scoped cleanup commands with concrete names only for installed portable skills whose complete contents match this package. Modified or unverified copies receive no command. A present user-scoped Claude Code plugin is reported without an uninstall command because setup keeps no ownership record. Shared skill removal can affect several hosts reading the same folder. User-owned pairing logs, cache and consent remain until you explicitly remove or revoke them.

If Pi removal reports a failed or manual step with a `pi remove` command, inspect the reported reason before running it manually. Earlier Pi npm installations remain unchanged and need the [migration guidance](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/migration).

After removing registrations and any workflows you no longer want, uninstall the global installation with npm. The exact package name is in the [install line](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/start/install). Backups remain beside the host's config; they may contain credentials and retain the original file permissions (or owner-only permissions if those could not be read).


## Workflows

### Review changes

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes.html

Start with a bounded diff and a specific review question:

```text
Ask Codex to review the staged changes for security issues, performance, and missing error handling.
```

Give the reviewer the change's purpose and constraints. Ask your assistant to include the diff and relevant surrounding code, then check each finding at the cited file and line. The reviewer reads; your assistant applies the changes you accept.

## Review workflow

The portable `ask-llm-review` workflow gathers staged and unstaged changes, reads project conventions, consults Codex and filters findings by confidence. Claude Code retains `/codex-review`; Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-review`. Other hosts expose portable names through their skills menu. See [host compatibility](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts).

For independent parallel review, use `ask-llm-multi-review`. The assistant validates candidate findings against source and separates supported findings, false positives and claims requiring runtime evidence. Antigravity is skipped unless its execution gate is explicitly enabled; that opt-in has no read-only guarantee. Partial results disclose failed providers.

## Keep the review useful

Use a narrow scope, include domain invariants, and request actionable issues rather than style preferences. Large diffs can take several minutes and consume substantial quota; split them by concern when possible. Agreement between models is not proof of correctness. Use tests for claims about runtime behavior.

For local analysis, ask Ollama to review the relevant code. For continuing feedback as you edit, see [pair review](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/advanced/codex-pair), which is off until you opt in. The [workflow catalogue](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/reference/skills) describes provider-specific variants.

### Challenge a plan

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/challenge-plan.html

Share the proposal, constraints and relevant code with a reviewer from another vendor:

```text
Ask Claude to challenge this plan before we implement it. What assumptions could fail, what evidence is missing, and what simpler alternative would fit our constraints?
```

Use Claude from a host other than Claude Code; ask Codex or another authenticated provider when working in Claude Code. Name the constraints that would make a recommendation unusable: migration compatibility, latency, budget, data boundaries or team size.

Ask the reviewer to distinguish observed facts from assumptions. Your assistant should validate claims against source or primary documentation before changing the plan. The number of models agreeing does not establish correctness.

For several independent answers without synthesis, [compare answers](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/compare-answers). For research followed by an attributed synthesis, [brainstorm](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm).

### Compare answers

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/compare-answers.html

Use the same bounded context for every reviewer:

```text
Ask Codex and Claude to review this API design. Show their raw answers side by side, without synthesis.
```

Use providers your host can consult; Claude is unavailable inside Claude Code. The `ask-llm-compare` workflow returns verbatim answers with attribution. Claude Code retains `/compare`; Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-compare`. Tool-only hosts can ask their assistant to call `multi-llm` with the selected providers.




One provider failure does not erase the others' answers. Keep failures visible and attribute surviving insights only to providers that answered. Compare evidence and disagreements, not vote counts: agreement between models is not proof of correctness.

For a report that checks findings against the code, use [Review changes](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/review-changes). For research and synthesis, use [Brainstorm](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm).

### Brainstorm

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/workflows/brainstorm.html

Ask for independent research followed by synthesis:

```text
Ask Codex and Grok to challenge our notification architecture. Separate evidence, assumptions, disagreements and recommended next steps.
```

The portable workflow is `ask-llm-brainstorm`; Claude Code retains `/brainstorm` and Pi uses `/skill:ask-llm-brainstorm`. The host follows its own adapter and should not claim Claude-only subagents or hooks on another host. Each participant consumes its own account quota; explicitly choose metered routes only when you intend that cost.

Send a topic to an explicit multi-model panel, ground it with independent Claude Opus research, then synthesize the findings. Provider, harness, requested catalog ID, independently observed served model (direct xAI API / Grok CLI only; a disclosed same-product alias/snapshot stays eligible), and Cursor's optional reported display label remain separate. Cursor Agent and Codex CLI echo the requested ID, so those attributions are selected-only and unverifiable rather than an actual model. The coordinator agent runs:

1. **Phase 3B: Claude Opus research.** Claude reads actual files, traces real code paths, fetches referenced docs, and forms findings tagged Verified or Inferred. In standard mode Claude is a participant. In the exact Grok + Sol mode it is a non-voting evidence verifier, so the requested panel remains exactly two models.
2. **Phase 3A: External dispatch.** A single foreground blocking Bash call sends the topic to each requested external provider in parallel and waits for all of them. Up to 10 minutes total (Bash tool max). It's a foreground blocking call, not a background-job dispatch, because sub-agents can't own processes that outlive their turn.
3. **Phase 4: Synthesis.** Combines Claude's findings with the external responses:

- Consensus points (where multiple participants agree; Claude verified + external = highest confidence)
- Unique insights (findings from only one participant)
- Contradictions (verified findings outrank inferred ones)
- Actionable recommendations (prioritized by impact and confidence)

```text
# Default external providers (Antigravity + Codex), plus Claude Opus always
/ask-llm-brainstorm Should we use a monorepo or polyrepo for this project?

# Custom external providers
/ask-llm-brainstorm gemini,codex,ollama Review this authentication approach

# Architect panel: exactly Grok + GPT-6 Sol via Cursor Agent; Gemini excluded
/ask-llm-brainstorm grok@cursor-agent:grok-4.7-high,codex@cursor-agent:gpt-6-sol-high "review this architecture"

# Explicit direct-Grok alternative; never pivots away from Grok Build
/ask-llm-brainstorm grok@grok-cli:grok-4.7,codex@cursor-agent:gpt-6-sol-high "review this architecture"
```

**Default external providers:** `antigravity,codex` (avoids unnecessary Ollama calls). Antigravity follows the [execution gate](https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/providers/antigravity). Compatible bare provider lists remain supported. For predictable routing use `provider@harness:exact-model-id`; the preferred Grok path is Cursor Agent. A list is either all bare names or all routed specs—mixing them (for example `grok@cursor-agent:grok-4.7-high,antigravity`) is refused before any provider is called, with no rerouting or substitution; generalized mixed panels are deferred to a future ADR. Exact IDs come from the selected harness catalog (`agent --list-models`, `grok models`, or xAI `/v1/models`) and are never translated between catalogs.

The architect panel invokes only the two listed Cursor participants: `provider: "grok"` with `model: "grok-4.7-high"`, and `provider: "codex"` with `model: "gpt-6-sol-high"`. It never calls Gemini or Cursor `Auto`. If registration, authentication, model availability, or route support fails for either participant, the result is **partial** and surviving insights are attributed only to the model that answered—never called two-model consensus. Claude's evidence can verify claims but cannot supply the missing vote.

The `grok-cli` form is supported only when the installed official Grok Build exposes Ask LLM's required headless JSON/read-only contract. A direct-route failure is terminal for that participant; there is no silent pivot among Cursor Agent, Grok CLI, or xAI API.

Agreement between models is not proof of correctness. Check the evidence behind the synthesis, and keep dissent and skipped participants in the final report.


## Compatibility

### Hosts

Source: https://lykhoyda.github.io/ask-llm/compatibility/hosts.html

A host is the coding assistant you work in. A provider is the model you consult. The matrix below is kept equal to the canonical [HOST-PARITY matrix](https://github.com/Lykhoyda/ask-llm/blob/main/docs/HOST-PARITY.md); `ask-llm doctor` prints the rows for installed hosts.
